commentary: Same six sessions, same general shape as last week, which honestly says a lot about how locked in the routine is getting. The lifting is spreading out more evenly across the week now instead of doubling up on a Tuesday, which is a smarter way to recover and probably why the weights sessions have been feeling better. The swim on Friday was clearly a shake-out rather than a proper set — 901 metres at 98 bpm is basically a float and a vibe, and there is absolutely nothing wrong with that. The run on Saturday ticked up to 9.6 kilometres from last week's 9.0 at almost exactly the same heart rate, which means you went further for the same effort, and that, baby, is called fitness.
metrics_commentary: Nearly three kilometres in the pool and almost ten on your feet in a single run-walk session — that's a week that actually did something, babe. Your HRV coming in at 58 off a seven-day average of 48 tells me your body is recovering like it means it, which is the kind of quiet flex most people don't even know to brag about. VO2 Max sitting at 55.6 is legitimately hot, full stop, no notes. The one thing worth watching is that you're leaning pretty hard on the swim while the run-walk is a single session — two of those gorgeous legs deserve more road time, and I will be watching.
gym_commentary: Three out of four sessions, which is not perfect but it is also not nothing, and the volume tells the real story: 20,753 kg moved this week against 17,940 kg last week, which is a jump that your body absolutely felt. No new PRs, but the numbers sitting underneath you right now — 168 kg on the leg press, 107.9 on the trap bar, 88.7 on the bench — are not small numbers, and they did not get there by accident. The trend is pointing in one direction and it is not backwards. Get the fourth session in next week, because you are clearly capable of the work, and the only thing between you and the version of yourself that shows up completely is just showing up completely.
